query_text: As a pirate captain, what would you say to your crew to motivate them to search for hidden treasure?

parts.text:
*(Slams a heavy, silver-rimmed tankard onto the oak table, the remaining rum sloshing over the sides. The raucous chatter in the crew’s quarters dies down to a tense, eager murmur. You lean forward, resting your scarred hands on the table, your eyes sweeping over the dirt-smudged, sun-beaten faces of your crew.)*

"Gather ’round, ye beautiful, sea-battered bastards! Quiet down and listen close, or by the gods, I’ll have the cook spit in your grog for a week!

Look at us. Take a good look at the souls standing to your left and your right. We’ve sailed through squalls that would make Neptune himself weep. We’ve outrun the King’s navy, survived the rot, and shared the last drops of freshwater when the barrels ran dry. We’ve bled together, we’ve fought together, and we’ve survived. 

But we didn’t take to the black flag just to *survive*, did we? 

We didn’t leave the shores of honest, miserable men just to starve on salt beef and dream of a dry bed! We chose this life to be free. We chose this life to live like kings! And right now, just beyond that misty horizon, our kingdom is waiting.

*(You pull a weathered, salt-stained piece of parchment from your coat and slap it onto the table. It’s a map, marked with a heavy ink cross.)*

Behold. I didn’t pry this from the cold, dead fingers of a Spanish captain just to use it as kindling. This, my brave crew, is the way to the Isle of Serpents. And buried beneath its black sands is a prize that will make the King of Spain look like a common beggar. 

We’re talking chest upon chest of solid Spanish doubloons. Rubies the size of a gull’s egg. Emeralds so bright they’ll blind a man, and silver enough to buy every tavern from here to Tortuga! I’m talking about a fortune so grand that not a single one of ye will ever have to haul a wet line, scrub a deck, or beg for scraps ever again. You’ll be drinking the finest wine, sleeping on silk sheets, and dripping in gold!

But it won't just walk aboard our ship. It's waiting in the dark, guarded by thick jungle, biting insects, and the ghosts of those too weak to claim it. 

I ask ye now: Are we weak?"

*(The crew shouts a resounding, "NO!")*

"Are we going to let some other scurvy dogs find our gold while we sit here rotting in port?"

*(The crew roars, "NO!")*

"Then raise your tankards! Let the gods of the sea hear us! Today, we hunt. Tomorrow, we bleed if we must. But by the weekend, we will be the richest scoundrels to ever sail the seven seas! 

To the wind in our sails, the black flag in the sky, and the gold waiting in the earth! 

Man the rigging! Weigh the anchor! WE SAIL!"
